Subject: Data residency & region pinning - follow-up from call

Thanks again for your time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap
- Primary ask: ensure EU data for EU customers and US data for US customers (data residency).
- DR/Failover: you want the ability for cross-region failover for DR but only if it preserves residency commitments and compliance posture.
- Backups: must be encrypted and stored in-region by default; replication to secondary region only with explicit approval.
- Logs & Audit: you need access to audit logs and the ability to ship them to your SIEM; retention policies vary by dataset.
- PII controls: preference for either pre-ingest redaction or tokenization; want options documented.

Proposed next steps
1) Sean to provide a technical note on region pinning, failover behavior, and backup replication options (see attached FAQ and architecture diagram).
2) Marissa to coordinate a technical workshop with your security/compliance folks — propose next week.
3) We'll produce a short mutual action plan (MAP) mapping your requirements to Redwood capabilities and timelines.

Attachments: region-pinning-faq.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
Links: https://redwood.ai/docs/region-pinning

Please confirm if the recap captures everything and share any additional constraints (e.g., specific EU countries to lock to, data classification levels, or regulatory guardrails).

Thanks Marissa — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- EU residency must cover both processing and storage for EU customer data (we're primarily concerned with the UK & Ireland and Germany).
- For backups: we are open to cross-region replication for DR but it must be encrypted in transit and at rest; copies outside the primary region require a documented exception and retention policy.
- Cross-region failover is acceptable provided logs and audit trails remain accessible to our security team and we can demonstrate chain-of-custody.
- We'd also like to understand whether Private (VPC) deployment is required or if Redwood's hosted offering can meet these controls with contractual commitments.

Can Sean and team outline the exact guarantees (e.g., whether KV cache or temporary artifacts are ever routed through a different region) and any configuration knobs we should be aware of? Also please include a short summary we can share with our legal/compliance teams.

Thanks — I'll get our InfoSec lead (cc'ing once scheduled) lined up for the workshop.

Hi Lisa / Tom — answering the technical asks below. I've kept this at a level your security folks can share with compliance; happy to go deeper in the workshop.

Region pinning & processing
- Per-customer and per-dataset region pinning: supported. You can pin a workspace, model deployment, and associated KV cache to a specific region (US, EU, APAC).
- Runtime behavior: inference is executed in-region for pinned workloads. Temporary caches (KV cache) remain in-region; we do not route model tokens through an external region during normal operation.

Cross-region failover
- Supported via warm-standby in a secondary region. Failover can be automated or manual.
- Failover involves starting a compatible model variant in the standby region; we replicate metadata and configuration to standby, but we do not replicate customer data to the standby unless replication is explicitly enabled.
- For DR scenarios where we must bring up a standby in another region, we offer an "emergency replication" workflow that requires a documented exception and customer sign-off.

Backups & replication
- Backups are encrypted (AES-256) and stored by default in the primary region.
- Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature (disabled by default) and will be surfaced in the MAP with retention windows and scope.

Logging & audit
- Audit logs can be retained in-region and exported to your SIEM (S3-compatible endpoint or Syslog over TLS).
- We can provide a retention policy table and a log access SLA for legal/compliance review.

PII controls
- Options: pre-ingest redaction pipeline, in-flight tokenization, or post-response redaction. We can run a short eval on your sample prompts/data to show redaction efficacy.

Next steps
1) I've attached a short architecture diagram and a data-retention table that maps Redwood artifacts to retention and default region behavior.
2) Proposed workshop: 60-90 minutes with your InfoSec + Platform + Legal; we'll walk architecture, MAP, and sign-off paths.
3) Marissa — can you propose 2 time slots next week?

Attachments: region-pinning-arch.png (PNG, 180KB), data-retention-table.csv (CSV, 12KB)
